candidates.name: Oral histoplasmosis
support_spans: Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
candidates.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts and a clean-based ulcer on the tongue suggests oral histoplasmosis.

candidates.name: Chronic traumatic ulcer
support_spans: No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
contradict_spans: The lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue, which gradually grew and subsequently ulcerated
candidates.why: The absence of a history of trauma makes chronic traumatic ulcer less likely.

candidates.name: Histoplasmosis
support_spans: Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
candidates.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts suggests a fungal infection, specifically histoplasmosis.

candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: The lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue, which gradually grew and subsequently ulcerated
contradict_spans: No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
candidates.why: The gradual growth and ulceration of the lesion could suggest a malignant process, such as squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: Histoplasmosis
support_spans: Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
Special stains (Grocott-Gomori methenamine-silver nitrate and periodic acid–Schiff) highlighted fungal forms
candidates.why: The presence of fungal forms on special stains and the negative fungal culture suggest histoplasmosis.

candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Histopathological examination (3-mm punch biopsy from edge of ulcer)
contradict_spans: Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils
candidates.why: The histopathological examination could confirm the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma.
